discovery: Spin qubits in semiconductors: the concept and realization of quantum bits encoded in single electron and nuclear spins in semiconductor quantum dots and donors

nominees.name: Bruce E. Kane
nominees.affiliation: Laboratory for Physical Sciences and University of Maryland, USA

nominees.name: Lieven M. K. Vandersypen
nominees.affiliation: QuTech and Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

subfield: Condensed matter physics / quantum information (semiconductor quantum devices)
motivation: Loss (with DiVincenzo, 1998) proposed encoding qubits in single electron spins in quantum dots, controlled by electrical gates and exchange coupling. In the same year Kane proposed nuclear-spin qubits on individual phosphorus donors in silicon. Together these two proposals set out a route to quantum computing built on the semiconductor technology that underpins modern electronics. Vandersypen turned the concept into experimental physics, with single-shot spin readout, coherent single-spin control by electric-dipole spin resonance, and high-fidelity two-qubit gates and multi-qubit processors in silicon/germanium. This work showed that single spins in solids can be isolated, controlled and entangled with precision. It opened a field that now achieves fault-tolerance-level fidelities in isotopically purified silicon. It also brought quantum coherence into CMOS-compatible, industrially scalable devices. This is fundamental physics that has become a new technology platform.
